bugs.title: Discount code applied twice when Apply is double-clicked
bugs.description: Double-clicking Apply in the basket's Discount code field applies the same single-use code twice, so the order total is reduced by twice the advertised discount.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Add any full-price item to the basket.
2. Enter the discount code SPRING10.
3. Double-click Apply.
4. Review the order summary.
bugs.expected_result: The code is applied once and the summary shows a single 10% discount line.
bugs.actual_result: Two 10% discount lines are shown and the total is reduced by 20%. The double discount is kept when the order is placed.

bugs.title: Checkout layout is broken in Internet Explorer 11
bugs.description: The checkout page renders as a single unstyled column in Internet Explorer 11. The Continue to payment button is obscured by the footer, preventing customers from proceeding with checkout.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Open the storefront in Internet Explorer 11.
2. Add any item to the basket.
3. Select Checkout.
bugs.expected_result: Checkout is usable, or the customer is told that the browser is not supported.
bugs.actual_result: The checkout page displays without its intended styling, and the Continue to payment button is inaccessible. Customers cannot proceed to payment.

bugs.title: Basket is emptied after returning from the payment page with browser Back
bugs.description: A customer reported through support that their basket was empty after they used the browser Back button on the payment page. The customer could not provide an order reference or the time of the attempt.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Add two items to the basket.
2. Proceed to the payment page.
3. Select the browser Back button.
4. Open the basket.
bugs.expected_result: The basket still contains both items.
bugs.actual_result: According to the customer, the basket was empty. Repeated attempts on Safari 26, Chrome 152 and Firefox 153 kept both items in the basket.

bugs.title: Order confirmation email shows the wrong delivery date for weekend orders
bugs.description: For orders placed on Saturday or Sunday with Standard delivery, the confirmation email shows an earlier estimated delivery date than the date displayed at checkout.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. On Saturday or Sunday, place an order using Standard delivery (3-5 working days).
2. Note the estimated delivery date on the order confirmation page.
3. Open the order confirmation email.
bugs.expected_result: The email and checkout confirmation display the same estimated delivery date.
bugs.actual_result: The email shows a delivery date one day earlier for Sunday orders and two days earlier for Saturday orders.

bugs.title: Free delivery is not applied to a basket of exactly £50.00
bugs.description: A basket totalling exactly £50.00 is charged the standard delivery fee. The site-wide banner reads "Free delivery on orders over £50".
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Add items totalling exactly £50.00 to the basket.
2. Proceed to checkout.
3. Select Standard delivery.
bugs.actual_result: A £3.99 Standard delivery fee is added to the order total.

bugs.title: Password reset link is rejected as expired when opened immediately
bugs.description: Some customers see "This link has expired" when they open a password reset link within a minute of requesting it. Support received six reports this week, all from Android devices.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. On an Android phone, select Forgot password and enter a registered email address.
2. Within one minute, open the reset email in the device's mail app.
3. Select Reset password.
bugs.expected_result: The password reset form opens. Reset links are valid for 60 minutes.
bugs.actual_result: The page shows "This link has expired". Requesting a second link usually works.

bugs.title: Product images have no alternative text on product detail pages
bugs.environment: Staging, NVDA screen reader with Firefox 153, Windows 11
bugs.description: Product gallery images on product detail pages have empty alt attributes, so NVDA skips them. Screen reader users cannot tell which product, colour or view each image shows.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Start the NVDA screen reader.
2. Open a product detail page with more than one gallery image.
3. Use NVDA's browse mode to navigate through the gallery content.
bugs.expected_result: Each image is announced with a short description, for example "Canvas backpack, navy, front view".
bugs.actual_result: NVDA skips the gallery images, so their product, colour and view information is not available to screen reader users.

bugs.title: VAT is calculated on the pre-discount price in the order summary
bugs.description: For business accounts, whose prices are shown excluding VAT, the VAT line in the order summary is calculated from the original price instead of the discounted price. The customer is overcharged.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Sign in with a business test account.
2. Add an item priced £100.00 excluding VAT to the basket.
3. Apply the 20% discount code SAVE20.
4. Review the order summary.

bugs.title: Stock level is not refreshed after the last item is sold
bugs.description: When the last unit of a product is bought, other customers already viewing the product page still see "In stock" and can add it to their basket. The problem is only reported at the payment step.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. In the admin panel, set a test product's stock to 1.
2. Open the product page in two separate browser sessions, A and B.
3. In session A, buy the product.
4. In session B, without reloading, select Add to basket and proceed to payment.
bugs.expected_result: Session B shows that the product is out of stock no later than the basket stage.
bugs.actual_result: Session B can add the product and reach the payment page, where "Item no longer available" is shown.

bugs.title: Customer is charged twice when 3-D Secure verification times out
bugs.environment: Production, card payments with 3-D Secure, all browsers
bugs.description: When 3-D Secure verification times out and the customer retries payment, two payments are captured for the same purchase, but only one order is created. Finance has confirmed four affected orders since the 2.4.0 release.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. In the payment provider's sandbox, select a test card that requires 3-D Secure.
2. At checkout, wait until the verification window times out (about 5 minutes).
3. Select Try again and complete the verification.
4. Compare the captured payments in the sandbox transaction log with the orders created.
bugs.expected_result: Only one payment is captured for the order. The timed-out payment attempt does not result in an additional charge.
bugs.actual_result: Two payments for the full order amount are captured, but only one order is created. The customer is charged twice.

bugs.title: Order history pagination skips the eleventh order
bugs.description: In My account > Order history, customers with more than 10 orders never see their eleventh most recent order: page 2 starts with the twelfth.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Sign in as a test customer with at least 12 orders.
2. Open My account > Order history.
3. Note the last order on page 1.
4. Open page 2.
bugs.expected_result: Page 2 starts with the order immediately after the last order on page 1.
bugs.actual_result: One order is skipped between page 1 and page 2.

bugs.title: Address lookup overwrites a manually corrected postcode
bugs.description: After a customer corrects the postcode returned by the address lookup, changing the delivery option runs the lookup again and restores the original postcode without warning. If the customer doesn't notice the change before placing the order, the incorrect postcode could result in a failed or misdirected delivery.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. At checkout, enter postcode AB12 3CD and select an address from the lookup results.
2. Change the postcode field to AB12 3CE.
3. Change the delivery option from Standard to Express.
bugs.expected_result: The corrected postcode AB12 3CE is kept.
bugs.actual_result: The postcode reverts to AB12 3CD and no message is shown.

bugs.title: Filters panel cannot be closed on iOS Safari
bugs.description: On category pages in iOS Safari, once the Filters panel is open, neither the Close button nor tapping outside the panel closes it. Customers have to reload the page to see the products.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. On an iPhone, open any category page in Safari.
2. Tap Filters.
3. Tap the Close (X) button.
bugs.expected_result: The panel closes and the filtered product list is shown.
bugs.actual_result: The panel stays open and the page behind it cannot be scrolled.

bugs.title: Homepage Autumn Sale banner contains a spelling mistake
bugs.description: A homepage promotional banner for the Autumn Sale displays “AUTUMN SLAE” instead of “AUTUMN SALE” in staging. The promotional campaign is scheduled to launch that day, requiring the banner to be corrected before launch.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Open the staging storefront.
2. Navigate to the homepage.
3. Inspect the Autumn Sale promotional banner.

bugs.title: Newsletter sign-up accepts an email address without a domain
bugs.description: The newsletter sign-up form in the site footer accepts addresses such as anna@ and shows the success message, although no confirmation email can be sent to them.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Scroll to the site footer.
2. Enter anna@ in the Newsletter email field.
3. Select Sign up.
bugs.expected_result: An inline error asks for a complete email address, and the address is not saved.
bugs.actual_result: "Thanks for signing up!" is shown and the address is saved.
